messages:
Anya: Heads up — invoice preview dashboards just spiked for a subset of prod tenants after yesterday's priority-routing rollout. Not full invoices, but preview token counts jumped ~3x for some accounts :eyes:
Marcos: Hmm, which routing change? the new priority allocator (PR #7342) that tags requests with route_priority=high?
Anya: Yep. I noticed it around 08:17 UTC when the canary moved from 10%->50%. Dashboard: /dashboards/preview/invoice/segmented shows the jump.
Devon: Possible cause: route tag propagation changed the fingerprinting key that upstream uses to dedupe streaming events. If fingerprint differs we double-count until aggregation window closes.
Kevin: Can you paste the raw event from the ingest side for an affected tenant? I want to see route tags and request_id correlation.
Anya: Pasted sample from the event stream: ```json
{"tenant_id":"acme-123","request_id":"r_9f2","route_priority":"high","fingerprint":"fp_7a3","tokens":120} 
{"tenant_id":"acme-123","request_id":"r_9f2","route_priority":"normal","fingerprint":"fp_1b9","tokens":120}``` 
Marcos: Whoa — same request_id but two different fingerprints depending on route_priority. That explains counting twice. Fingerprint derivation must include route tags now.
Devon: We intentionally added route_priority to fingerprint context to avoid mixing high/low priority accounting, but we didn't consider preview pipeline which dedupes by request_id+fingerprint. Bug.
Kevin: Impact: preview shows inflated counts until aggregate-window dedupe can reconcile. Real invoices might be fine if ledger dedupes differently, but preview UX is broken.
Anya: Alert got noisy: metering-bot sent 12 alerts between 08:20-08:30. metering-bot: "preview token delta > threshold for 18 tenants"
metering-bot: @eng-platform detected preview delta spike, created ticket MET-912
Marcos: Short-term mitigation: revert the fingerprint change in the canary or add a compatibility path in preview pipeline to ignore route_priority for fingerprinting. Which is faster?
Devon: Revert is fastest but painful for anyone relying on priority-aware accounting. Alternative: in preview aggregation add a normalization step: prefer request_id when present, otherwise compute fingerprint. That keeps preview stable.
Kevin: I can whip up a patch to preview postproc to prefer request_id dedupe. Pseudocode: ```sql
-- aggregator pseudo-query
SELECT request_id, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM preview_events
WHERE event_time >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY request_id;```
Marcos: That should drop duplicates caused by fingerprint differences. But watch edge cases where request_id absent for streaming legacy clients.
Anya: Agreed. Also need to update dashboard annotation and callout: "Known preview inflation during priority-routing rollout" so CS doesn't panic.
Devon: I'll open a follow-up to restore route_priority to fingerprint derivation but gate it with a feature flag so preview and ledger can adopt on schedule.
Kevin: Patch deployed to preview postproc canary at 08:55 UTC. After that the preview delta dropped ~95% within one aggregation window.
Anya: Verified on dashboards — preview now matches ledger-derived sanity checks for the top 20 tenants.
Marcos: Next steps: (1) Track MET-912 until we have feature-flagged rollout for fingerprint change, (2) add unit test to preview dedupe for mixed fingerprints, (3) update rollout playbook to include a preview-check after any routing-tagging changes.
Kevin: I'll update the runbook and add a short smoke test: run the sample script that emits same request_id with two different route_priority values and assert preview tokens remain deduped.
Anya: Thanks team — saved a lot of customer confusion. :pray: Filing a postmortem-lite in the channel later today with timeline and dashboards.
Devon: And note for telemetry: add metric preview.fingerprint_mismatch.count to detect this class of divergence automatically.
Marcos: Good call. I'll own the feature-flag PR and coordinate with Product for a controlled rollout.
Anya: Closing the loop — MET-912 updated with mitigation and owners. If anyone sees another unexplained preview spike ping here.
